headline: Exact identity correspondence for all 28,926 binary coordinates after relaxing 11,935 integrality declarations and deleting 3,270 rows (2,940 empty tautologies, 320 opposite-inequality partners with 320 L->E sense flips, 10 aggregate equalities): 4 claims, 595,373 obligations, 103,475 steps (11,200 Int Cases + 58,035 Lin + 34,240 EqPair), 45.6 MiB RPA -> 33.2 MiB RPX, VERIFIED in 4.4 s, work 29,858,280 of the 1e9 budget, peak_live_facts 12,585.

source.families: all 28,926 columns binary, every one given an explicit UP=1 inside a single INTORG/INTEND interval; 23,294 rows = 1,379 E / 10,537 L / 11,378 G; 2,940 rows are empty 0<=1; 320 L rows have an exact opposite partner; 11,200 u in 320 linking groups of 35; 735 w/gapday unit-coefficient definitions
source.evidence: /tmp/rpx-digests/test50.md report section 1 and eval Surveying MPS sections

target.edits: 11,935 integrality relaxations (u/w/gapday, [0,1] bounds kept); 3,270 row deletions in three audit classes; 320 senses L->E proved by EqPair; only serialization otherwise (NAME, INTORG->BV, zero RHS omitted)

row_delete_comparison.question: test50 deletes 3,270 rows with no column change while test42 deletes 166,500 and test33 90,000 - does one API shape cover all three?

test50.discharge: empty -> literal 'Exact' (no step); partner -> 1-term Lin at scale +-1 against the kept row now typed E; aggregate -> one mixed-sign integer combination of 36-47 retained rows; 1,280 partner Lin + 20 aggregate Lin over the two reverse claims

test33.discharge: each deleted row is a coefficient-1 sum of a path of 3-7 retained inequalities of the same sense; linear_steps_by_claim [0,90000,0,90000] = exactly one flat step per deleted row per reverse claim
test33.evidence: cases/test33/README.md (transitive implication paragraph) / cases/test33/preparation.json counts / tools/prepare_affine.py:117-118

test42.discharge: fixed activations: 2-term Lin over VarUpper/VarLower; the rest reference shared bisection Local facts (297 steps per 100 links), so 166,500 deletions cost 383,586 steps, about 2.3 emitted steps per row

row_delete_comparison.verdict: Yes - one shape covers all three if a deletion record carries its justification as a term list [(Ref,Rational)] whose Ref may be a retained row, a variable bound or a previously derived Local fact: test33's path is that list with all coefficients 1, test42's leaf is 1-2 Local/Row terms, test50's partner is one term at scale +-1, its aggregate is a mixed-sign list, and its 2,940 tautologies are the empty list already discharged as 'Exact'. Three things the shape must carry for the union: (a) test50 couples each partner deletion to a sense flip, so the edit list needs SetRowSense and the forward claim owes an EqPair rule (640 EqPair steps), not a combination; (b) sharing is not optional - test42 only affords 166,500 restorations because 110,100 of them are Local references (kernel peak_live_facts 383,586), while test50 spells every combination flat; (c) scale, not shape, is the binding constraint: flat per-row combinations cost test42 145.9 MiB (57% of the 256 MiB text cap) and sibling test36 254.8 MiB (99.5%).

claims: claim0 forward integer (reverse=false, input_integers=output_integers=true), identity map on all 28,926 coordinates with a 28,926-pair projection, inverse=claim1; 152,720 obligations (tools/prepare_test50.py:61-79).

claim1 reverse integer (reverse=true): proves 11,935 implied-integrality facts plus the 3,270 row restorations; 167,925 obligations, the only claim containing the 11,200 Int Cases blocks (tools/prepare_test50.py:21-45,61).

claim2/claim3: the same pair with input_integers=output_integers=false (continuous relaxation), 135,729 and 138,999 obligations; 152,720-135,729=16,991 and 167,925-138,999=28,926 are exactly the VarInt obligations dropped.
kernel wording: all four integer/LP identity mapping claims with all 28,926 original coordinates and the objective preserved, both complete compositions checked (cases/test50/README.md).

The objective is checked as 'Equal' per claim plus one appended 'Exact'; the two inverse identities are declared as integer indexes into the claim list ([1,0,3,2][len(claims)], tools/prepare_test50.py:82).
proof_encoding: RPA 2 text = 'RPA 2'+newline+one-line JSON {claims[4],blocks[4]}: 47,843,897 bytes (45.6 MiB, 18% of the 256 MiB text cap) -> proof.rpx 34,781,823 bytes, assembled in 0.41 s, verified in 4.40 s execute / 4.62 s total.

Node census counted in cases/test50/proof.rpa: 11,200 Cases, 58,035 Lin, 34,240 EqPair, 22,400 Witness branch ends, 0 Absurd, 0 points, 0 bijections; kernel statistics confirm branches=11200 and every other generated-* counter at 0.

Integrality sub-proofs are 100,800 of the 103,475 steps (97.4%): 11,200 Cases with 2 branches each, 5 Lin and 3 EqPair per Cases (56,000/33,600); the remainder is 735 unit-definition Lin(Int) + 1,280 partner Lin + 20 aggregate Lin.

Verified facts: 595,373 obligations, 10,281,115 linear terms, 1,160,504 substitution terms, peak_live_facts 12,585, work 29,858,280 (3% of the 1e9 default), i.e. budgets were never the binding constraint in this case.

Only Lin/Cases/EqPair nodes and RowEq/RowUpper/RowLower/VarLower/VarUpper/VarInt/Local/Assumption references are used; no Flow/Interval/Menu/Injective/Signed/Plotkin node appears (kernel statistics all 0).
agent_manual_work: Two independent exact MPS readers written by hand (Fraction first pass, Decimal row-oriented cross-check) with a full section survey: 23,295 ROWS, 268,607 COLUMNS, 21,117 RHS, 28,926 BOUNDS records, one INTORG interval (digest report section 2).

Name-free structural discovery of the 320 linking groups: 35 u per group, disjoint Z_t partitions matching the exact support of a retained c1 count equality, k in 1..4, k equal to the count RHS (digest eval Proving auxiliary integrality and aggregate identities).

The implied-integrality case analysis itself (x=0 forces every u=0 by nonnegativity; x=1 makes every slack u_t-s_t zero), worked out by hand and then encoded as Cases/Lin steps (digest report section 3).

Ten aggregate combination certificates solved for by hand as weighted c11 partition equations cancelling the x coefficients, stored as explicit 36-47-row integer combinations in proof_certificates.json redundant_equalities.

Falsification work the kernel never sees: the y1/y2 unit-definition attempt (coefficients 2/3/4, exact local 1/2 point), the exhaustive scan finding 0 of 90 c6a/c6b opposite pairs, the duplicate scan and the one-component incidence check (digest eval Testing scope limits and reduction counts).
preparer_helpers: prepare_test50.cases_int (tools/prepare_test50.py:13-18): a hand-written Int-kind Cases emitter that rebuilds the node dict and the {'Assumption': len(builder.assumptions)} indices, because prepare_test88.Builder.cases is Eq-kind only (tools/prepare_test88.py:47-56).

prepare_affine.parse_mps (57 lines, tools/prepare_affine.py:20-76) + row_ref/get_fact (77-88): the only model readback the generator has, called on both the 24 MB source and the agent's rewritten MPS.
prepare_test40.expression/plus/mul/expr_json/row_fact (tools/prepare_test40.py:72-90): the (constant,terms) rational algebra every Lin term list is built from, with rows as RHS-negated expressions.

prepare_test54.fact/exact (tools/prepare_test54.py:16-22): the shortcut that turns a single-term combination into a bare row reference, or a vacuous obligation into the literal 'Exact' used for all 2,940 empty rows.
prepare_test57.substitute (tools/prepare_test57.py:11-19) spliced in for variable-to-expression substitution on rows and the objective, replacing the simpler copy in prepare_test40 for term counts.
friction: The deleted-row class is invisible in the API: it is recovered by set difference (tools/prepare_test50.py:55) and then each class needs its own hand-written expression in the check loop (66-75), so nothing forbids a class from being discharged by the wrong rule.

All four claims carry a full copy of the model-level obligation list (595,373 obligations; the same 4x28,926 bound checks) and the identity projection is spelled out as 28,926 pairs per claim, so 1,530,980 of request.json's 1,531,420 bytes are boilerplate.

The inverse pairing is claim-index arithmetic ([1,0,3,2][len(claims)], line 82) rather than a named claim id, and the claim quad is an inline nested loop (lines 75-84) - reordering requires re-deriving the permutation.
Attack mutations are dict pokes into the emitted JSON (lines 95-98) and each materialises a full 45.6 MB .rpa plus 33.2 MB .rpx inside cases/test50 (four mutations, ~315 MB retained).

Failure attribution is manual: wrong_opposite_pair and missing_active_balance were both recorded as 'INVALID equality pair' with only status+message in the receipt (preparation.json negative_checks), so the rule-broken prose at line 93 is authored, not checked.

notes: Budget posture: RPA 45.6 of 256 MiB, work 29.9M of 1e9, live facts 12,585 of 1e6 - this case is not resource-bound; it is bound by hand-written rule plumbing (97.4% of its steps are Int Cases/Lin/EqPair re-deriving 11,935 dropped integrality declarations) and by 1.53 MB of identity-projection boilerplate. Cross-case row deletion: one deletion record with a [(Ref,Rational)] justification covers test50's 3,270 (trivial/1-term/mixed-sign), test33's 90,000 (coefficient-1 paths) and test42's 166,500 (Local-fact trees), provided the record also carries the coupled sense flip and the Ref union includes Local facts; what does not transfer is cost - test33 spends exactly 1 step per deleted row, test42 ~2.3 with sharing, and test50 pays nothing extra per deleted row because its 11,200 Int Cases dominate.
